title: Cooperative Domain-Wall Dynamics in a Two-Dimensional Quasiclassical Holstein Model
authors: Arunangshu Bora, Sankha Subhra Bakshi, Ho Jang, Gia-Wei Chern
abstract: We investigate charge-density-wave (CDW) coarsening in a two-dimensional quasiclassical Holstein model following thermal quenches into the ordered phase. Although the staggered CDW order parameter is nonconserved, domain-wall motion remains constrained by conservation of the microscopic electronic charge. The simulations exhibit apparent growth exponents between $1/4$ and the Allen--Cahn value $1/2$. These apparent exponents are primarily accounted for by the crossover kinetics $\dot{L}=[D(T)/L][1+L_\times^2(T)/L^2]$, where $L_\times(T)$ is a temperature-dependent crossover length. At low temperature, nearly binary occupations require compatible wall segments to rearrange cooperatively, producing the $L(t)\sim t^{1/4}$ limit. Thermal broadening creates partially occupied interfacial sites that permit local curvature-driven motion and restore $L(t)\sim t^{1/2}$ at late times. Fits to the measured growth rate, a dimensionless rate collapse, and a long-time large-system simulation consistently support this crossover picture. These results show that a microscopic conservation law can generate long-lived anomalous coarsening even when the emergent order parameter is nonconserved.
summary: This work analyzes the coarsening of charge-density waves in a 2D quasiclassical Holstein model after a thermal quench. It reveals that while the order parameter is nonconserved, microscopic charge conservation forces the domain growth to follow an anomalous $t^{1/4}$ law at low temperatures. This behavior smoothly crosses over to the expected $t^{1/2}$ law at higher temperatures, demonstrating the profound influence of microscopic constraints on macroscopic dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how charge-density-wave (CDW) coarsening dynamics proceed in two dimensions following a thermal quench into the ordered phase, particularly focusing on the constraints imposed by microscopic charge conservation.
main_result: The dynamics exhibit a crossover between two regimes: a low-temperature, charge-conserving limit leading to $L(t) \sim t^{1/4}$, and a high-temperature, curvature-driven limit restoring $L(t) \sim t^{1/2}$.
method: The research employs quasiclassical approximations and Langevin simulations on the Holstein model to track the evolution of domain-wall size $L(t)$.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the two-dimensional quasiclassical Holstein model, which couples lattice vibrations ($Q_i$) to electronic charge density ($n_i$). The dynamics are governed by a Langevin equation for the lattice coordinates.
key_observables: Domain growth length scale $L(t)$, and the apparent power-law exponents characterizing the coarsening kinetics.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), the crossover length scale $L_	imes(T)$, and the ratio of cooperative to local contributions.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the quasiclassical limit, treating lattice motion as slow compared to fast electronic dynamics, and assuming rapid electronic relaxation to quasi-equilibrium.
figures_summary: The analysis relies on fitting measured growth rates and performing dimensionless rate collapses to confirm the crossover picture between different power-law behaviors.
paper_structure: The paper develops the quasiclassical Hamiltonian and equations of motion, simulates the thermal quench protocol, analyzes the resulting correlation functions to define $L(t)$, and finally discusses the crossover kinetics linking the $t^{1/4}$ and $t^{1/2}$ regimes.
why_interesting: The interplay between emergent order parameters (CDW) and underlying microscopic conservation laws provides a rich example of non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, relevant to understanding phase separation in cuprates or manganites.
